text: I failed my first technical interview and it crushed me. But that failure forced me to finally focus on fundamentals instead of shortcuts.
Nobody talks about how confusing the first month of learning to code really feels. If you're struggling, you're not behind — you're learning.
If I had to restart my tech career, I would stop watching endless tutorials and start building projects from day one.
One mistake I made early in my career was focusing too much on tools instead of understanding the basics.
Your first project will be messy. Your second will be better. Progress comes from building, not waiting for perfection.
Learning to code is not about being smart. It's about being patient and consistent when nothing seems to work.
Every expert was once a beginner who decided not to quit.
Stop waiting to feel ready. You will never feel ready. Start anyway.
Your career grows faster when you share what you're learning instead of waiting to be perfect.
Small daily improvements beat massive motivation every single time.
